notes: Policy covers Colorado, Kansas, and Utah facilities with different FPL bands and copay structures.
Colorado has separate tables for insured and uninsured patients; Kansas and Utah tables do not distinguish insurance status.
Colorado uninsured 0-250% FPL receives free care ($0 copay, 0% of charges).
Insured patient copayments cannot be lower than the 0-250% (Colorado/Utah) or 0-150% (Kansas) copay amounts.
Uninsured patient copayments cannot be lower than the 0-250% insured copay amounts (Colorado).
Provider fees are listed separately from facility fees for each state.
Utah provider fees reference 'Holy Cross Hospitals' while Colorado references 'CommonSpirit Provider Fees'.
Policy references compliance with PPACA/501(r) and Colorado Senate Bill 14-50.
Screening for financial assistance offered to uninsured patients when possible.
Emergency/urgent patients treated regardless of ability to pay or coverage status.
Documentation requirements, application procedures, and covered facility/provider lists are in addenda not provided.
Service exclusions (cosmetic, transplant, research) not specified in provided text.
Application deadline for financial assistance not specified in days from service or first statement.
Payment plan terms (max months, max % of income, min payment) not specified beyond 'reasonable options'.
0 may leave out a condition: Claim misses that the 30-day period starts after payment due date, not first post-discharge bill.

findings.title: Covers everyone Colorado's Hospital Discounted Care protects

law.source: HCPF Hospital Discounted Care Operations Manual, Mar 31 2026
law.quote: Patients and their households are eligible for Hospital Discounted Care if, during the required screening and application processes, they are determined to: Have a total household income at or below 250% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines (FPG), and Be residents of the State of Colorado.
IF REQUESTED BY THE PATIENT, A HEALTH-CARE FACILITY SHALL SCREEN AN INSURED PATIENT FOR DISCOUNTED CARE

findings.summary: Inconclusive: 35 of the model's rules were dropped by the quote and meaning checks, so a missing rule may be our error. Z3's case: A household of 3 earning $41,000 a year (150.1% of the poverty line), living in Colorado, uninsured meets every requirement, but no rule of this policy grants them help. Colorado law makes them eligible for Hospital Discounted Care.
